messages.text: explain the error the cause and what can we do differently

The browser’s LocalStorage is tiny—think "text notes," not photo albums. When you attach an image, the code currently stores it as a base64 data URL (those `data:image/jpeg;base64,/9j/4AAQ...` strings). Base64 encoding bloats binary data by about one-third, so a 2.5 MB photo becomes ~3.3 MB. Add a few of those and you slam into the browser’s storage wall (usually 5 MB on mobile Safari, sometimes 10 MB on desktop). **What we can do differently:** 1. **Compress before saving**: Draw the image onto an HTML canvas, resize it so the longest edge is max 800 pixels, then export as JPEG at 80% quality. This typically shrinks a 4 MB photo down to 200–400 KB—well under the limit. 2. **Defer heavy storage**: Keep using LocalStorage for task text/tags, but move images to IndexedDB (R2 scope) which gives you megabytes or gigabytes of space. For now, compression keeps us in R1 without adding new dependencies. 3. **Guard rails**: Check the estimated payload size before calling `setItem`. If it’s too big, warn the user and don’t crash the app. **The fix in plain terms**: Instead of `reader.readAsDataURL(file)` → save directly, we’ll: - Load the image into an `` tag - Draw that to a `` resized to 800px max - Call `canvas.toDataURL('image/jpeg', 0.8)` to get a compressed base64 string - Save that smaller string When you’re ready, say **"build it"** and I’ll add the canvas compression logic to the image handler. ℹ No file written — answer only. !
